title_en: Relevant Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Reporting and Approval of Judicial Review Cases Concerning Arbitration

articles.content_en:
Article 2 Any intermediate people's court or special people's court handling an arbitration judicial review case involving foreign, Hong Kong, Macao, or Taiwan elements shall report to the Higher People's Court in its jurisdiction for review if, after examination, it intends to determine that the arbitration agreement is invalid, or refuse to enforce or set aside an arbitral award rendered by an arbitration institution in the mainland of China, or refuse to recognize and enforce an arbitral award rendered in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, the Macao Special Administrative Region, or the Taiwan region, or refuse to recognize and enforce a foreign arbitral award; if the Higher People's Court, after examination, intends to approve, it shall report to the Supreme People's Court for review. Only after review by the Supreme People's Court may it render a ruling in accordance with the review opinion of the Supreme People's Court.
Any intermediate people's court or special people's court handling an arbitration judicial review case not involving foreign, Hong Kong, Macao, or Taiwan elements shall report to the Higher People's Court in its jurisdiction for review if, after examination, it intends to determine that the arbitration agreement is invalid, or refuse to enforce or set aside an arbitral award rendered by an arbitration institution in the mainland of China; only after review by the Higher People's Court may it render a ruling in accordance with the review opinion of the Higher People's Court.

Article 3 For an arbitration judicial review case not involving foreign, Hong Kong, Macao, or Taiwan elements as specified in paragraph 2 of Article 2 of these Provisions, if the Higher People's Court, after examination, intends to approve the intermediate people's court's or special people's court's refusal to enforce or setting aside of an arbitral award rendered by an arbitration institution in the mainland of China on the ground that it violates social public interest, it shall report to the Supreme People's Court for review; only after review by the Supreme People's Court may it render a ruling in accordance with the review opinion of the Supreme People's Court.

Article 4 For cases reviewed by the Higher People's Court pursuant to paragraph 2 of Article 2 of these Provisions, the Higher People's Court shall, within fifteen days from the date of rendering the review opinion, report to the Supreme People's Court for the record.

Article 5 When a lower people's court submits a case to a higher people's court for review, it shall submit the written report together with the case file materials. The written report shall set forth the review opinion and the specific reasons.

Article 6 After receiving the application for review from the lower people's court, if the higher people's court considers that the relevant facts of the case are unclear, it may inquire of the parties, or return the case to the lower people's court for supplementary investigation of the facts and subsequent resubmission.
Article 7 The higher people's court shall, in the form of a reply letter, provide the review opinion to the lower people's court.

Article 8 In civil action cases, where a party refuses to accept a ruling made by the people's court concerning the validity of an arbitration agreement, such as a ruling refusing to accept the case, a ruling rejecting the prosecution, or a ruling on a jurisdiction objection, and files an appeal, and the second-instance people's court, after examination, intends to determine that the arbitration agreement was not established, is invalid, has ceased to have effect, or has unclear content, making it impossible to perform, it must report level by level for review in accordance with Article 2 of these Provisions, and only after review by the higher people's court may it render a ruling in accordance with the review opinion of the higher people's court.

Article 9 These Provisions shall come into force as of January 1, 2018. If any judicial interpretation previously issued by this Court is inconsistent with these Provisions, these Provisions shall prevail.
